name: Seizure-cooling brain implant
subtitle: a thin film that chills seizures early

effects.effect: an electric field makes certain thin films heat up or cool down
a device whose resistance remembers how much current passed through it

effect: an electric field makes certain thin films heat up or cool down
how: A third of people with epilepsy get no relief from drugs, and cooling a patch of brain by a few degrees is known to stop a seizure from spreading. Electrodes on the brain's surface pick up the electrical storm starting, a memristor chip that has learned this patient's warning pattern flags it using almost no power, and a voltage across a paper-thin film makes the film go cold over the trouble spot until the storm passes.
obstacle: The heat the film pulls out has to be dumped somewhere without warming the brain next to it.
why: Cooling stops seizures in animal studies; electrocaloric films have never been put in a body.
real: Focal brain-cooling implants for epilepsy use thermoelectric (Peltier) or passive cooling; electrocaloric cooling appears only as a listed candidate mechanism in an implant-cooling review.
